newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA INTERBANK MARKET RATES (CHIBOR) MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CHINA INTERBANK MARKET RATES (CHIBOR) MIXED.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Tuesday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell to 685 million yuan from 750 million yuan on Monday with the one-day contract the most actively traded.
Dealers said trading remained dull due to a lack of fresh market-mvoing factors after rumours of a possible cut in bank reserve ratios caused trading to slow on Monday.
Both state banks and non-banking financial institutions were reluctant to trade due to market uncertainty triggered by the rumours, they said.
The bank reserve ratio, the sum Chinese banks must deposit with the central bank as a proportion of total deposits, now stands at 13 percent.
Rumours of a cut have circulated on the market periodically since July last year, when the central bank said it was considering a cut in the reserve ratio.
Officials have declined to comment on a timetable.
Traders said they expected the interbank rates to move in a very narrow range in slow trading in the short term because of the market uncertainty.
